name: keytracked low-osc bass split with wet delay
goal: Make a simple expressive patch where delay can dominate the mix, and a low oscillator’s level is key-tracked so bass appears mainly in the left-hand/low register while upper notes stay clearer.

source.title: TRAVELER | Behind the Scenes with David Helpling

prerequisites: Synth with key-tracking to oscillator level, and a wettable delay

inputs.name: delay_wet
inputs.description: High wet so delay nearly louder than dry

constraints: Original synthesis only; not affiliated with KeySolutions; do not rip Traveler samples/presets/wavetables.
Original synthesis only — design new patches from portable parameters; do not copy proprietary Traveler factory preset names, banks, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with KeySolutions Sounds or Traveler; concepts mapped to generic hybrid-synth / Web Audio equivalents.
Do not rip, dump, or redistribute Traveler content.
Prefer recreating the described signal-flow and motion relationships in our browser music system or any hybrid synth with comparable modules.

steps.action: Create a simple two-layer patch: mid/high tonal oscillator(s) plus a dedicated low oscillator.
steps.expect: Both layers audible in low register

steps.action: Modulate the low oscillator’s volume with keyboard tracking so it is strong only in the lower register (left hand / low keys) and fades as you play higher.
Set delay wet very high (delay almost louder than the dry sound) to showcase modulation/space; filter delay feedback to taste.

verification: High keys thin out the low osc
